summary.title: How to Use OpenAPI and Swagger for Documentation
summary.one_liner: The page is a ReadMe product landing page, not a tutorial, so it shows what ReadMe offers for turning OpenAPI/Swagger specs into interactive API docs rather than teaching the topic itself.
keywords: api docs from yaml or json
takeaways: ReadMe can generate an interactive API reference with code samples and auth handling from an uploaded OpenAPI spec.
A spec can be imported by drag and drop, by URL, or synced from GitHub or GitLab repositories.
ReadMe also offers a visual API Designer for building an API reference without writing an OpenAPI spec.
The page is product marketing; it does not itself teach how to write OpenAPI or Swagger documents.
summary.summary: Despite the article title in the listing, the page text is a ReadMe marketing page covering its documentation platform. It shows an example OpenAPI JSON document with a single path (/pet/{id}) and how ReadMe renders it as an interactive API reference. It also lists features such as Git sync, AI linting, a visual API designer, multilingual docs, and enterprise controls, with customer quotes and compliance claims. Little general how-to guidance on OpenAPI or Swagger is present.
